scenario_stem:
Redcliff Brickworks is a private limited company founded 7 years ago, manufacturing clay bricks at a single yard staffed by 70 production workers and 6 truck drivers. Annual revenue reached $3.1 million last year. Managing director Vera Okafor makes every decision personally, setting a daily target of 48,000 bricks and approving each overtime roster herself. There is no staff representative body, and workers say they are never asked for their views.

The company has just won a $900,000 contract to supply bricks for a supermarket development, requiring 60,000 bricks per day for 9 weeks. A union organiser has since approached the workforce, citing 2 forklift accidents last year linked to rushed, unconsulted instructions. The board must decide between keeping Vera's autocratic style to hit the deadline or introducing daily democratic briefings where workers suggest safer methods. Faster decisions favour Vera's approach, but safety and morale favour consultation.
